records.source: עוּרִ֥י עוּרִ֛י לִבְשִׁ֥י עֻזֵּ֖ךְ צִיּ֑וֹן לִבְשִׁ֣י׀בִּגְדֵ֣י תִפְאַרְתֵּ֗ךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ עִ֣יר הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ כִּ֣י לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֛יף יָבֹא־בָ֥ךְ ע֖וֹד עָרֵ֥ל וְטָמֵֽא׃
records.gloss: Awake, awake, put on your strength, O Zion; put on [the] garments of your beauty, O Jerusalem, the city of the holiness; for not again will come into you anymore uncircumcised and unclean.
pieces: Wake up, wake up, Zion; wrap yourself in your strength! \q Jerusalem, holy city, dress in your robes of beauty, \q for never again will anyone uncircumcised or unclean come into you.

L.1: Awake, awake, put on your strength, Zion; \q put on the garments of your beauty, Jerusalem, city of holiness; \q for [the] uncircumcised and [the] unclean will no longer come into you again.

R.1: Wake up, wake up, people of Zion! Be strong again. \q People of Jerusalem, the holy city, put on your most beautiful clothes. \q No one who is uncircumcised or unclean will ever come into your city again.

decisions.choice: awake, awake: the call that Zion made to God's arm is now made to Zion
decisions.reason: In 51:9 the people cried to the arm of the LORD, "Awake, awake, put on strength", and in 51:17 Jerusalem was told to rouse herself from the cup of wrath. Now God answers with the same doubled words: it is Zion who must wake and dress for what he is about to do.

decisions.choice: put on your strength ... garments of your beauty: take up again the strength and honor that belong to you
decisions.reason: Qualities are pictured as clothing (59:17; 61:10; Psalm 93:1). Zion has been sitting in mourning and shame; now she is to dress as a city restored to honor.

decisions.choice: the uncircumcised and the unclean: those outside God's covenant who invaded and defiled the city
decisions.reason: Foreign armies had entered Jerusalem and its temple (64:10; Psalm 79:1; Lamentations 1:10). The promise is that the holy city will not be profaned again (Joel 4:17). Revelation 21:27 says nothing unclean will enter the new Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: people of Zion ... Be strong again ... People of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the people for the city addressed (as at 40:9) and says plainly what putting on strength means.

records.heading: Zion, rise from the dust

records.source: הִתְנַעֲרִ֧י מֵעָפָ֛ר ק֥וּמִי שְּׁבִ֖י יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם הִֽתְפַּתְּחִי֙ מוֹסְרֵ֣י צַוָּארֵ֔ךְ שְׁבִיָּ֖ה בַּת־צִיּֽוֹן׃ס
records.gloss: Shake yourself free from [the] dust, arise, O captive Jerusalem; loosen for yourself the bonds of your neck, O captive daughter of Zion.
pieces: Shake the dust from yourself and stand, Jerusalem, held captive! \q Undo the cords that bind your neck, captive Daughter Zion.

L.2: Shake yourself free of the dust; get up, captive Jerusalem; \q free yourself from the bonds of your neck, captive daughter of Zion.

R.2: People of Jerusalem, you are prisoners, but shake off the dust and stand up! \q People of Zion, untie the ropes from around your necks.

decisions.choice: captive: Jerusalem as a prisoner, matching "captive daughter of Zion" in the next line
decisions.reason: The same letters can be read as the command "sit" (from the verb meaning to sit or dwell), giving "arise, sit [on your throne], Jerusalem". The parallel with "captive daughter of Zion" favors "captive", and it is how the source data reads the word.

decisions.choice: loose for yourself: the reading of the margin (qere)
alternatives: the bonds of your neck have come loose
decisions.reason: The written text (ketiv) has a third-person plural form, "the bonds of your neck have come loose". The margin reads a command to Zion, "loose the bonds", which fits the other commands in the verse. The sense is the same: her captivity is ending.

decisions.choice: shake yourself from the dust: Zion rises from mourning and shame
decisions.reason: Sitting in the dust is the posture of grief and humiliation (3:26; Lamentations 2:10). In 47:1 Daughter Babylon was told to come down and sit in the dust; now Zion is told to rise from it. The fortunes of the two cities are reversed.

decisions.choice: People of Jerusalem ... People of Zion
decisions.reason: Readable names the people for "Jerusalem" and "daughter of Zion" (see the note on Daughter Zion at 1:8).

records.source: כִּֽי־כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה חִנָּ֖ם נִמְכַּרְתֶּ֑ם וְלֹ֥א בְכֶ֖סֶף תִּגָּאֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh: For nothing you were sold, and not with money you will be redeemed.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: You were sold and nothing was paid; you will be redeemed and no silver will change hands.

L.3: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: For nothing you were sold, and not with money will you be redeemed.

R.3: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: When you were sold, no one paid anything for you. So you will be bought back without any money.

decisions.choice: sold for nothing: God handed his people over to their enemies without receiving any price
decisions.reason: Israel was given up because of its sins (50:1), not in payment of a debt. Since no one paid for them, no one has a claim that must be bought out; God can take them back freely (45:13).

decisions.choice: redeemed without money: set free by God's own act, with no ransom paid
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a relative who buys back a family member or property (Leviticus 25:25, 47-49). Here no payment is made: the LORD frees them by his power (verse 10). The word for money is the word for silver.

records.source: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה מִצְרַ֛יִם יָֽרַד־עַמִּ֥י בָרִֽאשֹׁנָ֖ה לָג֣וּר שָׁ֑ם וְאַשּׁ֖וּר בְּאֶ֥פֶס עֲשָׁקֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: [To] Egypt went down my people at the first to sojourn there, and Assyria for nothing oppressed it.
pieces: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Long ago {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people went down to Egypt to stay there as foreigners; then Assyria crushed them without cause.

L.4: For thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: To Egypt {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people went down at first to live there as aliens, and Assyria oppressed them without cause.

R.4: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Long ago {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people went to live in Egypt as strangers. Later, Assyria was cruel to them for no reason.

decisions.choice: Egypt and Assyria: two earlier oppressors of God's people
decisions.reason: Jacob's family went down to Egypt as guests (Genesis 46:3-4; 47:4) and were later enslaved there. Assyria destroyed the northern kingdom and invaded Judah (chapters 10; 36-37). Babylon, the present oppressor, is in view in verse 5.

decisions.choice: without cause: Assyria had no right to oppress them
decisions.reason: The phrase means "for nothing": Israel had done Assyria no wrong and Assyria paid nothing for them. It echoes "for nothing" in verses 3 and 5. It can also be read "at last", in contrast with "at first".

decisions.choice: Later
decisions.reason: Readable adds "Later" to show that Assyria came long after the time in Egypt, as the contrast with "at first" implies.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֤ה מַה־לִּי־פֹה֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־לֻקַּ֥ח עַמִּ֖י חִנָּ֑ם מֹשְׁלָ֤יו יְהֵילִ֨ילוּ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְתָמִ֥יד כָּל־הַיּ֖וֹם שְׁמִ֥י מִנֹּאָֽץ׃
records.gloss: And now, what [is] to me here? declares Yahweh, for my people has been taken for nothing; its rulers wail, declares Yahweh, and continually all the day my name [is] despised.
pieces: So now, what is here for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. My people have been taken, and nothing was paid for them. Their rulers howl, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all day long, without pause, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is scorned.

L.5: And now, what [do] I [have] here? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have been taken away for nothing; their rulers wail, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and continually, all the day, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is despised.

R.5: Now look at what has happened, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. My people were taken away, and no one paid anything for them. Their rulers cry out and howl, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. All day long, people insult {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

decisions.choice: what [do] I have here: the reading of the margin (qere)
decisions.reason: The written text (ketiv) has "who [is] to me here?"; the margin reads "what". God asks what he has gained, or what he is to do, now that his people are held captive. The sense of the verse is the same either way.

decisions.choice: their rulers wail: the leaders of God's people cry out in their distress
alternatives: those who rule over them howl in triumph
those who rule over them mock
decisions.reason: "Their" refers to "my people". The verb is the usual word for wailing in grief (13:6; 15:2). It may instead mean that the people's foreign rulers howl in triumph or mock them; the line is hard.

decisions.choice: my name is despised: the nations scorn the LORD because his people are captive
decisions.reason: When Israel is defeated, the nations conclude that its God is weak (Ezekiel 36:20-23). Romans 2:24 quotes this line in its Greek form, which reads (from memory, to be checked) "because of you my name is blasphemed among the nations".

decisions.choice: taken, and nothing was paid for them
decisions.reason: The word for "for nothing" is the one used in verse 3, where it means without a price. Balanced spells this out so the link is heard.

records.source: לָכֵ֛ן יֵדַ֥ע עַמִּ֖י שְׁמִ֑י לָכֵן֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כִּֽי־אֲנִי־ה֥וּא הַֽמְדַבֵּ֖ר הִנֵּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Therefore will know my people my name; therefore in the day the that, that I [am] he, the [one] speaking; here I [am].
pieces: That is why {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will come to know {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. That is why, on that day, they will know that I am {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, the one who speaks: Here I am!

L.6: Therefore {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will know {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name; therefore in that day [they will know] that I [am] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, the [one] who speaks: here I [am]!

R.6: So {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will know who I am. When that time comes, they will know that I alone am God. I am the one who promised this, and now I am here!

decisions.choice: my people will know my name: they will know by experience who the LORD is
decisions.reason: To know God's name is to know his character and power at first hand (Exodus 6:3-7; Psalm 9:11). Where the nations despise the name (verse 5), God's people will come to know it when he rescues them.

decisions.choice: I am he, the one who speaks: here I am: the God who promised is now present to act
decisions.reason: "I am he" is God's claim to be the one true God (see the note at 43:10). "Here I am" is what a servant says when he answers a call (6:8); here God says it to his people (58:9; 65:1). The words he spoke before are now fulfilled.

decisions.choice: I alone am God
decisions.reason: Readable says what "I am he" claims, as at 43:10.

decisions.choice: I am the one who promised this
decisions.reason: Readable takes "the one who speaks" as God's earlier promises, now kept (verse 3; 40:8). It may simply mean "I who am speaking now".

records.source: מַה־נָּאו֨וּ עַל־הֶהָרִ֜ים רַגְלֵ֣י מְבַשֵּׂ֗ר מַשְׁמִ֧יעַ שָׁל֛וֹם מְבַשֵּׂ֥ר ט֖וֹב מַשְׁמִ֣יעַ יְשׁוּעָ֑ה אֹמֵ֥ר לְצִיּ֖וֹן מָלַ֥ךְ אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: How lovely on the mountains [are the] feet of [one who] brings good news, [who] announces peace, [who] brings good news of good, [who] announces salvation, [who] says to Zion, Reigns your God!
pieces: What a welcome sight on the mountains, the feet of one who brings good news! He calls out peace, he brings word of good things, he announces salvation, \q and he tells Zion, "Your God reigns!"

L.7: How lovely on the mountains [are the] feet of [the] bearer of good news, announcing peace, bearing news of good, announcing salvation, \q saying to Zion, "Your God reigns!"

R.7: Look! A messenger with good news is coming over the mountains. How wonderful it is to see him! He announces peace. He brings good news. He tells everyone that God will save them. \q He says to the people of Zion, "Your God is King!"

decisions.choice: how lovely ... the feet: the runner's arrival is a welcome sight
decisions.reason: News came by runners. The watchers see the messenger's feet crossing the hills toward the city and know from his running that he brings word (2 Samuel 18:24-27). The feet stand for his coming.

decisions.choice: one who brings good news: a messenger announcing victory and rescue
decisions.reason: The same word is used in 40:9 and 41:27 (see the note at 40:9). Nahum 2:1 uses almost the same words of the messenger announcing Nineveh's fall. Paul quotes this verse of those who preach the gospel (Romans 10:15).

decisions.choice: Your God reigns: the LORD has shown himself king
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "has become king" or "is king". It is the cry of the psalms that celebrate God's rule (Psalm 93:1; 96:10; 97:1; 99:1). God's return to Zion (verse 8) shows to all that he rules.

decisions.choice: How wonderful it is to see him
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the lovely feet mean the joy of seeing the messenger arrive.

decisions.choice: Your God is King
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "reigns" means.

records.source: ק֥וֹל צֹפַ֛יִךְ נָ֥שְׂאוּ ק֖וֹל יַחְדָּ֣ו יְרַנֵּ֑נוּ כִּ֣י עַ֤יִן בְּעַ֨יִן֙ יִרְא֔וּ בְּשׁ֥וּב יְהוָ֖ה צִיּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: [The] voice of your watchmen! They lift up a voice; together they shout for joy, for eye to eye they will see when returns Yahweh [to] Zion.
pieces: Hear it! Your watchmen are raising a shout; they cry out for joy as one, \q for they see it plainly, eye to eye, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} comes back to Zion.

L.8: [The] voice of your watchmen! They lift up [their] voice; together they shout for joy, \q for eye to eye they will see {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} return [to] Zion.

R.8: Listen! The watchmen on the city walls are shouting. They are all singing for joy together. \q They can clearly see {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} coming back to Zion.

decisions.choice: watchmen: lookouts posted on the city walls
decisions.reason: Watchmen stood on the walls or towers to see who was approaching (21:6-8; 62:6; 2 Samuel 18:24-27). They are the first to see the messenger of verse 7 and the LORD coming behind him.

decisions.choice: eye to eye: directly and clearly, close at hand
decisions.reason: The phrase is used in Numbers 14:14 of the LORD being seen face to face among his people. The watchmen see his return with nothing hidden.

decisions.choice: the LORD returns to Zion
decisions.reason: The LORD, who left his city when it fell (Ezekiel 10-11), comes back to it (40:9-11; Ezekiel 43:1-5). The words could also be read "when the LORD restores Zion" (compare Psalm 126:1).

decisions.choice: on the city walls
decisions.reason: Readable says where watchmen stood, so the picture is clear.

records.source: פִּצְח֤וּ רַנְּנוּ֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו חָרְב֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּֽי־נִחַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ עַמּ֔וֹ גָּאַ֖ל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: Break forth, shout for joy together, O ruins of Jerusalem, for has comforted Yahweh his people; he has redeemed Jerusalem.
pieces: You ruined places of Jerusalem, break into song; shout for joy, all of you together! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has brought comfort to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has redeemed Jerusalem.

L.9: Break out, sing for joy together, ruins of Jerusalem, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has comforted {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has redeemed Jerusalem.

R.9: Ruins of Jerusalem, shout and sing for joy together! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has comforted {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. \q He has bought back Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the LORD has comforted his people: the comfort promised at 40:1 has come
decisions.reason: The second half of Isaiah opens with "Comfort, comfort my people" (40:1), and the theme returns in 49:13 and 51:3, 12. Here the comfort is announced as done.

decisions.choice: has comforted ... has redeemed: future rescue spoken of as already accomplished
decisions.reason: The verbs are past in form, though Jerusalem still lies in ruins. The prophet speaks of what God will do as so certain that it can be told as done (compare 44:23; 49:13).

decisions.choice: ruins of Jerusalem: the city's ruined places, told to sing
decisions.reason: Jerusalem was destroyed by Babylon in 587 BC. The ruins themselves are called to rejoice, as mountains and trees are elsewhere (44:23; 49:13; 55:12).

records.source: חָשַׂ֤ף יְהוָה֙ אֶת־זְר֣וֹעַ קָדְשׁ֔וֹ לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְרָאוּ֙ כָּל־אַפְסֵי־אָ֔רֶץ אֵ֖ת יְשׁוּעַ֥ת אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ס
records.gloss: Has bared Yahweh the arm of his holiness to the eyes of all the nations, and will see all [the] ends of [the] earth the salvation of our God.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has stripped bare {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy arm in full view of every nation, \q and the whole earth, to its farthest edges, will see the salvation of our God.

L.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has bared {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy arm before the eyes of all the nations, \q and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is ready to act. He has shown {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy power to all the nations. \q People in the farthest places on earth will see how our God saves.

decisions.choice: bared his holy arm: God gets ready to act in power
decisions.reason: A warrior or worker pulls back his robe to free his arm for action (Ezekiel 4:7). God's arm stands for his strength to rescue (40:10; 51:9; 53:1). "Holy" marks the power as God's own.

decisions.choice: all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God
decisions.reason: Psalm 98:2-3 uses the same words: "all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God." What God does for Zion is done before the whole world (40:5; 49:6).

decisions.choice: is ready to act ... has shown his holy power
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of baring the arm instead of reproducing it.

decisions.choice: how our God saves
decisions.reason: Readable uses the verb "save" for the noun "salvation", as the settled wording allows.

records.source: ס֤וּרוּ ס֨וּרוּ֙ צְא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֔ם טָמֵ֖א אַל־תִּגָּ֑עוּ צְא֣וּ מִתּוֹכָ֔הּ הִבָּ֕רוּ נֹשְׂאֵ֖י כְּלֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Depart, depart, go out from there; unclean do not touch; go out from its midst; purify yourselves, [you who] carry the vessels of Yahweh.
pieces: Depart, depart, get out of there! \q Touch nothing unclean. \q Leave from the midst of her and make yourselves pure, \q you who bear the vessels of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.11: Depart, depart, go out from there! \q Do not touch [anything] unclean; \q go out from the midst of her; \q purify yourselves, [you who] carry the vessels of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.11: Leave! Leave! Get out of Babylon! \q Do not touch anything unclean. \q Get out of that city and make yourselves pure, \q you who carry the things used to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: from there ... from her midst: from Babylon
decisions.reason: The place is not named here, but 48:20 has the same call: "Go out from Babylon." Paul applies the call to believers in 2 Corinthians 6:17: come out and be separate, and touch nothing unclean.

decisions.choice: the vessels of the LORD: the temple's sacred vessels, carried home
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar took the temple vessels to Babylon (2 Kings 25:13-15), and Cyrus sent them back with the returning exiles (Ezra 1:7-11). Only those set apart for it might carry holy things (Numbers 4:15), so the bearers must be pure.

decisions.choice: touch nothing unclean; purify yourselves: the departure is a holy procession
decisions.reason: The return home is pictured as a march of worship, not a flight. The people leave behind the uncleanness of an idol-worshiping land.

decisions.choice: Get out of Babylon
decisions.reason: Readable names the place, following 48:20.

records.heading: Go out and be pure

records.source: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א בְחִפָּזוֹן֙ תֵּצֵ֔אוּ וּבִמְנוּסָ֖ה לֹ֣א תֵלֵכ֑וּן כִּֽי־הֹלֵ֤ךְ לִפְנֵיכֶם֙ יְהוָ֔ה וּמְאַסִּפְכֶ֖ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: For not in haste will you go out, and in flight not you will go, for [is] going before you Yahweh, and your rear guard [is the] God of Israel.
pieces: For you will not leave in a rush, \q nor go off like runaways. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} walks at your head, \q and the God of Israel guards you from behind.

L.12: For not in haste will you go out, \q and in flight you will not go, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] going before you, \q and the God of Israel [is] your rear guard.

R.12: You will not have to hurry away or run for your lives. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will lead you, \q and the God of Israel will protect you from behind.

decisions.choice: not in haste: unlike the first exodus
decisions.reason: Israel ate the first Passover in haste and left Egypt in haste (Exodus 12:11; Deuteronomy 16:3). This going out will be calm and unhurried.

decisions.choice: going before you ... your rear guard: God leads and protects the march
decisions.reason: In the exodus the pillar of cloud went before Israel and then moved behind them to guard them (Exodus 13:21; 14:19). 58:8 uses the same word for rear guard.

records.source: הִנֵּ֥ה יַשְׂכִּ֖יל עַבְדִּ֑י יָר֧וּם וְנִשָּׂ֛א וְגָבַ֖הּ מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: Look, will act wisely my servant; he will be high and he will be lifted up, and he will be exalted exceedingly.
pieces: Look, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant will act with insight and succeed. \q He will rise and be lifted up; he will stand very high.

L.13: Look, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant will act wisely; \q he will be high and lifted up, and exalted exceedingly.

R.13: Look! My servant will do what is wise, and he will succeed. \q He will be raised up and honored. He will be given the highest place.

decisions.choice: my servant: the start of the song of the servant that runs to 53:12
decisions.reason: Verses 13-15 and chapter 53 form one poem about the servant who suffers and is exalted. On who the servant is, see the note at 41:8: the word can name the people Israel or a figure with a mission to them (49:5-6). This servant suffers for the sins of others (53:4-6). The New Testament reads the song as fulfilled in Jesus (Acts 8:32-35; 1 Peter 2:22-25).

decisions.choice: act wisely: act with insight and so succeed
decisions.reason: The verb means to have understanding and also to prosper as its result (Joshua 1:8; 1 Samuel 18:14-15). Jeremiah 23:5 uses it of the righteous king from David's line.

decisions.choice: high and lifted up: the words used of the Lord's throne
decisions.reason: Isaiah saw the Lord "high and lifted up" (6:1), and 57:15 calls God "the high and lifted up One". The servant, rejected and disfigured (52:14; 53:3), is raised to the same height.

decisions.choice: act with insight and succeed
decisions.reason: Balanced gives both sides of the verb, wise action and its success.

decisions.choice: He will be raised up and honored. He will be given the highest place.
decisions.reason: Readable says what being high and lifted up means: honor and the highest rank.

records.heading: The servant raised high

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁמְמ֤וּ עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ רַבִּ֔ים כֵּן־מִשְׁחַ֥ת מֵאִ֖ישׁ מַרְאֵ֑הוּ וְתֹאֲר֖וֹ מִבְּנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: Just as were appalled at you many, so [was] disfigured beyond a man his appearance, and his form beyond [the] sons of humankind,
pieces: Just as many stared at you in horror \q (his appearance so ruined it no longer seemed a man's, \q his form so marred it hardly looked human),

L.14: Just as many were appalled at you \q (so disfigured beyond [that of] a man [was] his appearance, \q and his form beyond [that of] the {{gender:children|sons}} of humankind),

R.14: Many people were shocked when they saw him. \q His face and body were so disfigured that he hardly looked human.

decisions.choice: at you: God turns for a moment to speak to the servant
decisions.reason: The poem speaks of the servant as "he" before and after this line. The sudden "you" is God addressing him directly. Some ancient versions read "at him" (the Syriac and the Targum, from memory, to be checked).

decisions.choice: disfigurement: the servant's appearance was ruined
decisions.reason: The Masoretic Text has a noun meaning "disfigurement". The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) has letters that can be read "I anointed" (from memory, to be checked), giving "I anointed his appearance beyond any man". The Masoretic reading fits the shock of the onlookers and 53:2-3.

decisions.choice: just as ... so: the comparison runs into verse 15
decisions.reason: "Just as many were appalled" is completed by "so he will sprinkle many nations" in verse 15. The words about his appearance are an aside explaining why they were appalled.

decisions.choice: when they saw him
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "him" throughout, since the sudden "you" refers to the same servant and would confuse a new reader.

decisions.choice: His face and body
decisions.reason: Readable uses "face" for his appearance and "body" for his form.

records.source: כֵּ֤ן יַזֶּה֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים עָלָ֛יו יִקְפְּצ֥וּ מְלָכִ֖ים פִּיהֶ֑ם כִּ֠י אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־סֻפַּ֤ר לָהֶם֙ רָא֔וּ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־שָׁמְע֖וּ הִתְבּוֹנָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: so he will sprinkle nations many; at him will shut kings their mouth, for what not had been recounted to them they will see, and what not they had heard they will understand.
pieces: so he will sprinkle many nations. \q Kings will fall silent before him, \q for they will see a thing no one ever told them \q and grasp a thing they never heard.

L.15: so he will sprinkle many nations; \q at him kings will shut their mouths, \q for what had not been told them they will see, \q and what they had not heard they will understand.

R.15: In the same way, he will sprinkle many nations to make them clean. \q Kings will be so amazed at him that they cannot speak. \q They will see things no one ever told them. \q They will understand things they never heard before.

decisions.choice: sprinkle: the priestly act of sprinkling to cleanse
decisions.reason: Everywhere else in the Bible this verb means to sprinkle blood, oil or water to make clean or holy (Leviticus 4:6; 14:7; 16:14). That suits a servant whose life is made a guilt offering (53:10). But here nothing is named as sprinkled, and the parallel with "appalled" in verse 14 suggests a meaning such as "startle", which the Septuagint's "many nations will marvel at him" supports (from memory, to be checked).

decisions.choice: kings will shut their mouths: they are struck silent with awe
decisions.reason: Shutting the mouth is the response of people overwhelmed by what they see (Job 29:9-10; Micah 7:16). Kings who once looked away from the servant now stand speechless before him.

decisions.choice: what they were not told they will see: news of the servant reaches those who never heard
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this line in its Greek form to explain why he preached where Christ had not been named (Romans 15:21).

decisions.choice: to make them clean
decisions.reason: Readable says why sprinkling was done in Israel's worship. Since the sense of the verb here is uncertain, this explanation is uncertain too.

decisions.choice: so amazed at him that they cannot speak
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of shutting the mouth.
